shortcut_name: Connected n-minus-one graph is a tree
evidence: deepseek: "Root at any target" and builds an adjacency list with DFS; gpt-oss: stores "parent" and "pw" for tree traversal; both immediately special-case "t == 1"
affordance_in_statement: The complete collection of m available operators is sufficient to guarantee that if their sum evaluates to zero, then all n coordinates of x must be identical. Furthermore, this collection contains exactly m = n - 1 operators, which is the exact rank required to enforce this one-dimensional solution space.
removal_suggestion: This cannot be removed under the immutable m = n - 1 and connectivity guarantees without changing the graph problem. If changing the task were permitted, allow arbitrary connected operator graphs instead of guaranteeing a connected n-minus-one edge set; otherwise only re-present the guarantee indirectly, which is unlikely to defeat tree-based solutions.

common_affordance: The operators form a connected graph with exactly n - 1 edges, so they form a tree with unique paths between targets.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The code is organized around generic DSU/Kruskal operations (find, union, rank), treating the task as an unrestricted connectivity or MST selection problem instead of selecting the unique minimal target-spanning subtree of the given tree.

The code likewise uses generic union-find state (parent and rank) rather than exploiting the unique tree paths and pruning edges outside the target subtree, so its connectivity-based selection can include or reject the wrong edges.

recommended_edit: To defeat both surviving approaches with one change, remove the explicit guarantee that the n - 1 operators are a connected sufficient set and make the operator graph arbitrary while retaining the same input format; this removes the tree/unique-path affordance. Under the stated immutable constraints, however, no semantics-preserving edit can remove this structural shortcut.
